newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares rise to new high on back of dollar.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares rise to new high on back of dollar.

text.p: Swedish shares closed at a record high on Tuesday, boosted by a stronger dollar and a lower than expected U.S. labour cost index.
The exchange's general index rose one percent to a record 2,525.75 in turnover of 4.2 billion crowns.
Fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz jumped 75 crowns to 1,115 ahead of its 1996 earnings report due on Thursday.
Appliance maker Electrolux gained four to 442, still benefiting from Monday's news that Atlas Copco chief executive Michael Treschow will become the head of Electrolux.
The forestry sector rose 2.04 percent on the strong dollar.
Pharmaceutical company Astra was boosted by figures that showed U.S. sales of its blockbuster anti-ulcer agent Losec rose by 40 percent last year and by general favourable trends.

The banking sector rose 1.11 percent with Nordbanken gaining two to 234 and S-E-Banken jumping 1.5 crowns to 74. The banks have been riding on merger speculation for months and hopes were rekindled last week when a newspaper report said the deal could be announced at the beginning of this week.
Telecoms group Ericsson rose 3.5 to 240.5 as it was pulled along in the general upturn, dealers said.
